svg.title: Terminal showing ReferenceError require is not defined in ES module scope with Node explanation
svg.desc: A terminal running node build.js. Node throws ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, you can use import instead. Node then explains that the file is treated as an ES module because it has a .js extension and package.json contains type: module, and that renaming it to .cjs would treat it as a CommonJS script. The error message states both the cause and two of the fixes.
svg.text: ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope, you can use import instead
This file is being treated as an ES module because it has a '.js' file extension
and '/app/package.json' contains "type": "module". To treat it as a CommonJS
script, rename it to use the '.cjs' file extension.
↑ Node states the cause and two fixes in the message itself — read past line one.
